question_text: A 52-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of a blistering rash in his inguinal region. Upon further questioning, he also endorses an unintended weight loss, diarrhea, polydipsia, and polyuria. A fingerstick glucose test shows elevated glucose even though this patient has no previous history of diabetes. After referral to an endocrinologist, the patient is found to have elevated serum glucagon and is diagnosed with glucagonoma. Which of the following is a function of glucagon?

Question: A 52-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of a blistering rash in his inguinal region. A fingerstick glucose test shows elevated glucose even though this patient has no previous history of diabetes. After referral to an endocrinologist, the patient is found to have elevated serum glucagon and is diagnosed with glucagonoma. Which of the following is a function of glucagon?

opb. Increased glycolysis
